In March 1969 British paratroopers and London police landed on Anguilla to end the breakaway that began with the Anguilla Revolution. No shots were fired.

The press mocked the operation as an invasion of a tiny island by a great power, the "Bay of Piglets". Yet many Anguillans welcomed the troops, since they wanted British rule, not rule from St Kitts.

A British commissioner took over, and Royal Engineers stayed to build roads and a pier. The landing led to the separation of Anguilla from the associated state and its own status in the British system.
sum: In March 1969 British paratroopers and London police landed on Anguilla to end the breakaway that began with the Anguilla Revolution. No shots were fired.
